title: K_0 class of a finite projective module with a finite free resolution
statement: Let $S$ be a commutative ring and let $L$ be a finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] $S$-module. Suppose there are an integer $d\ge0$, integers $r_0,\dots,r_d\ge0$ and an exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] of $S$-modules $0\to F_d\to\cdots\to F_1\to F_0\to L\to 0$ in which each $F_i$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with a basis of $r_i$ elements. Then $[L]=n[S]$ in $K_0(S)$ [def-trf-k0-group] for the integer $n=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^ir_i$; in particular $[L]=n[S]$ for some $n\in\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 0AFY (more-algebra-lemma-perfect-to-K-group), clauses (2) and (3), lines 36491 onward: a finite complex of finite projectives has alternating K_0 class

proof.text: Set $K_0=L$. For $1\le i\le d$, let $K_i$ be the image of $F_i\to F_{i-1}$ (equivalently the kernel of $F_{i-1}\to F_{i-2}$), and let $K_1$ be the kernel of $F_0\to L$. Exactness gives surjections $F_i\twoheadrightarrow K_i$ for $1\le i\le d$ and short exact sequences $0\to K_{i+1}\to F_i\to K_i\to0$ for $0\le i<d$, where the map for $i=0$ is $F_0\to L$ and $K_{d+1}$ is not needed. The map $F_d\to K_d$ is an isomorphism because the leftmost arrow is injective. This is precisely the kernel/image formulation of exactness.

source.place: Tag 0AFY, proof: represent the perfect object by a finite complex and use exactness of its terms; lines 36491--36558

proof.text: Inductively, every $K_i$ is finitely generated projective. The base $K_0=L$ is projective and finitely generated by hypothesis. If $K_i$ is projective, the surjection $F_i\twoheadrightarrow K_i$ lifts the identity of $K_i$ along the surjection by the projective lifting property, so the short exact sequence in Step 1 splits. Thus $K_{i+1}$ is a direct summand of the finite free module $F_i$, hence projective by the direct-summand characterization. It is finitely generated because projecting a finite basis of $F_i$ onto the summand gives finitely many generators. The same argument applies through $i=d-1$.

source.place: Tag 0AFY, proof: short exact sequences split because the quotient is projective; lines 36521--36548

proof.text: For each $0\le i<d$, a chosen splitting identifies $F_i$ with $K_{i+1}\oplus K_i$, while the leftmost isomorphism identifies $F_d$ with $K_d$. The current presentation of $K_0(S)$ is generated by isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective modules and imposes the direct-sum relation, so it gives $[F_i]=[K_{i+1}]+[K_i]$ for $i<d$ and $[F_d]=[K_d]$.

source.place: Tag 0AFY, proof: split short exact sequences and additivity in K_0; lines 36521--36558

proof.text: Taking the alternating sum of the equalities in Step 3 cancels the classes $[K_1],\ldots,[K_d]$ and leaves $[L]=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^i[F_i]$. A free module with a basis of $r_i$ elements is isomorphic to $S^{\oplus r_i}$, so the same direct-sum relation in the current $K_0(S)$ presentation gives $[F_i]=r_i[S]$. Hence $[L]=\left(\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^ir_i\right)[S]$, and the final assertion follows by taking this integer as $n$.

The current K_0 generators and direct-sum relation then telescope to the alternating sum of the free ranks. No new DAG node was needed because the splitting and direct-summand facts remain explicit in the cited projective-module and exact-sequence definitions.
